text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.1% today as oil prices climbed to their highest levels in months amid escalating U.S.-Iran tensions. Brent crude topped $101 a barrel—the strongest close since May—driven by concerns that fighting in the Persian Gulf could disrupt Middle East energy supplies. As an oil producer, ConocoPhillips benefits directly when crude prices rise, since higher oil commands better margins and revenue.

The stock's 3.6% gain over two weeks mirrors the broader rally in energy prices as geopolitical risk has mounted. With political uncertainty expected to keep energy elevated through the midterm elections, oil-dependent companies like this one remain supported by the price environment—though that same political backdrop also adds unpredictability to the outlook.
